label: lr-ae3cb
summary: The network combines four effects. A saddle in systolic pressure and heart rate: high pressure with a slow heart rate raises the predicted risk (an arm read as sbp / heart_rate, concept score 0.96), a fast heart rate without high pressure raises it through a shock gate (detector concept heart_rate > 76 and sbp < 145, score 0.97), and a brake that opens with a fast rate or high pressure cancels the direct terms, so a fast heart rate with high pressure is low risk (mean predicted risk 1.2% for the 38 training patients matching heart_rate > 90 and sbp > 145). A U in serum sodium with a flat bottom, steeper on the low side, where very low sodium also opens the shock gate (mean predicted risk 58.8% for sodium < 134, 28.0% for sodium >= 134 and sodium <= 139 and 53.1% for sodium > 139). Straight-line rises with age and creatinine through direct terms, and smaller additions for smoking, diabetes and male sex; body-mass index barely matters and the noise input is unconnected. The annotated model reproduces the network (function preservation error 1.8e-15) with full structural and compositional coverage.
